name: Canada
summary: Canada is not a contracting party to the 1958 UNECE Agreement. Under MVSR Schedule IV section 108 (CMVSS 108), passenger cars must comply with Technical Standards Document No. 108 (TSD 108, Rev. 8), which is based on FMVSS 108 (as of 2022-02-22) and allows UN regulations only as an alternative for headlamps. Compliance is self-certified by the vehicle manufacturer or importer (National Safety Mark on the vehicle's compliance label); rear lamps as separate parts are not 'equipment' under the Motor Vehicle Safety Act. For a rear lamp designed to UN R148/R48, you mainly need to prove US/Canadian photometry, mounting heights, red rear side marker lamps/side retro-reflectors and 3-year outdoor weathering of the plastic optics.

standards.id: MVSR C.R.C., c. 1038, Schedule IV, s. 108 (CMVSS 108)
standards.title: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations – Lighting Systems and Reflective Devices (Standard 108)
standards.scope: s. 108(1): passenger cars, MPVs, trucks, trailers and buses must comply with TSD 108 as amended from time to time. s. 108(5)-(8): UN R8, R20, R31, R98, R112 and R123 only as an alternative for headlamps, with the type approval, marking and CoP requirements of the UN regulations explicitly not applying. s. 108(16), (18), (19): Canada-specific activation rules for rear position lamps (e.g. when front fog lamps/rear fog lamp are switched on and in combination with daytime running lamps). s. 108(24): information required on the vehicle must be bilingual (English/French). Consolidated version, current to 2026-09-30.

standards.title: Technical Standards Document No. 108 – Lamps, Reflective Devices, and Associated Equipment
standards.scope: Adaptation of FMVSS 108 (49 CFR 571.108, as of 2022-02-22); published/effective 2025-04-01, mandatory from 2025-10-01. Applies only to original equipment (replacement equipment requirements S6.7 not adopted). Contains Table I-a (required lamps/reflectors for passenger cars), photometry for rear position lamp (Table VIII), stop lamp (Table IX), lighted area (Table IV-a), visibility (S6.4) and physical tests incl. plastic optics (S14.4.2) and vibration/moisture/dust/corrosion (S14.5).

standards.title: Motor Vehicle Safety Act
standards.scope: s. 3: National Safety Mark (may only be applied by companies authorised by the Minister); s. 5(1): compliance with the standards, evidence, marking and records of design, manufacture, testing and field performance as prerequisites for marking, sale and import; Schedule I defines 'equipment' only as tires and restraint systems for children/persons with disabilities – lamps are not separately regulated equipment.

standards.title: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations – National Safety Marks, Compliance Label, Records
standards.scope: s. 3: National Safety Mark (Schedule I) and authorisation by the Minister; s. 6: compliance label on the completed vehicle (manufacturer, date of manufacture, National Safety Mark with authorisation number, VIN, GVWR/GAWR, vehicle type, e.g. 'PC/VT'); s. 10: compliance records must be kept for at least 5 years.

certification.scheme: CMVSS / Motor Vehicle Safety Act – National Safety Mark
certification.marking: No component approval mark for rear lamps: the DOT marking requirements (S6.5.1) are deleted in TSD 108, and an E-mark is not required. The vehicle carries the compliance label with the manufacturer's National Safety Mark and authorisation number (MVSR s. 6).
certification.summary: Canada relies on self-certification: with the compliance label and the National Safety Mark, the vehicle manufacturer or importer confirms compliance with all CMVSS including CMVSS 108/TSD 108, and must keep records of design, testing and field performance (MVSA s. 5(1)(g), MVSR s. 10: at least 5 years). Transport Canada checks afterwards through vehicle tests and reviews of the certification documents. Rear lamps themselves are not 'equipment' under Schedule I of the MVSA; they are assessed only as part of the vehicle, i.e. the lamp supplier provides the TSD 108 evidence to the vehicle manufacturer.

notes: accepts_un_approvals=false: MVSR s. 108(1) requires compliance with TSD 108; UN regulations are allowed as a technical alternative only for headlamps (s. 108(5)-(7)), and even there the type approval and marking requirements of the UN regulations explicitly do not apply (s. 108(8)). There is no UN alternative for rear lamps (rear position, stop, reversing lamps, retro-reflectors). UN R48 comparison values are taken from the version published in OJ L 347 of 30.9.2021 (Supplement 1 to the 07 series of amendments); newer UN R48 versions were not checked. UN R148 photometry values were not retrieved, so CAN-05 only states the Canadian target values.

deviations.topic: No recognition of UN approvals for rear lamps
deviations.national_requirement: Passenger cars must meet TSD 108 (adaptation of FMVSS 108) (MVSR s. 108(1)). UN regulations are allowed as an alternative only for headlamps (s. 108(5)-(8)); there is no UN alternative for rear position, stop and reversing lamps or retro-reflectors. An E-approval under UN R148/R150 does not replace this evidence.
deviations.suggestion: Produce a test report against TSD 108 Rev. 8 (photometry, colour, physical tests under S14) for each function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) and provide it to the vehicle manufacturer as the basis for its self-certification.

deviations.topic: Marking: no DOT/E-mark required, National Safety Mark on the vehicle
deviations.national_requirement: TSD 108 deletes the DOT marking requirements (S6.5.1 incl. S6.5.1.2 for signal lamps and retro-reflectors); no approval mark is required on the lamp. Compliance is confirmed via the vehicle's compliance label with the National Safety Mark and authorisation number (MVSR s. 6, MVSA s. 3). Information required by law on the vehicle under s. 108 must be bilingual (English/French) (s. 108(24)).
deviations.suggestion: State in the marking specification that no component approval mark is needed for Canada, and add the TSD 108 declaration of conformity for the vehicle manufacturer to the delivery documentation; the E-mark can be kept for UN markets.

deviations.topic: Red rear side marker lamp and side retro-reflector mandatory
deviations.national_requirement: TSD 108 Table I-a requires for all passenger cars one red side marker lamp at the rear on each side ('as far to the rear as practicable', mounting height at least 380 mm, on with headlamps/parking lamps) and one red side retro-reflector at the rear on each side. UN R48 (07 series) requires side marker lamps and side retro-reflectors only on vehicles longer than 6 m (optional for shorter M1 vehicles, or only required if the geometric visibility of the position lamps is reduced).
deviations.suggestion: Integrate a red side marker lamp and a red side retro-reflector per TSD 108 S7.4/S8.1 into the rear lamp (side surface), or make sure the vehicle has these functions elsewhere on the rear side, and document this in the specification.

deviations.topic: Mounting heights and mounting on fixed body parts
deviations.national_requirement: TSD 108 Table I-a: rear position and stop lamps 380-1829 mm, retro-reflectors 380-1524 mm above ground (UN R48, 07 series: rear position/stop lamp 350-1500 mm, rear retro-reflector 250-900 mm). Under S6.1.3.2, rear position, stop and turn signal lamps on non-fixed parts (e.g. the tailgate) only count as supplementary lamps; the required functions must be provided on the fixed part.
deviations.suggestion: Check the mounting position: place retro-reflectors and all lamp functions at least 380 mm above the road (retro-reflectors max. 1524 mm), and put the required rear position/stop functions in the body-mounted part of the lamp (not in the tailgate).

deviations.topic: Separate photometry, lighted area and visibility requirements under TSD 108
deviations.national_requirement: Rear position lamp per Table VIII (1 lighted section: min. 2.0 cd at H-V, max. 18 cd), stop lamp per Table IX (1 lighted section: min. 80 cd at H-V, max. 300 cd; minimum stop/tail ratio of 5 or 3 per test point if optically combined), measured per S14.2.1 on the SAE test point grid with group totals. Stop lamp on passenger cars with at least 5000 mm² effective projected luminous lens area (Table IV-a, single-compartment lamp). Visibility per S6.4.3 (lens area option 1250 mm² or luminous intensity option).
deviations.suggestion: Add the target values from TSD 108 Tables VIII, IX and IV-a to the specification, have the photometry re-measured on the TSD test grid and adjust the optics or lighted area if values fall short; choose and document the visibility option under S6.4.3.

deviations.topic: Plastic optics: 3 years of outdoor weathering (Florida and Arizona)
deviations.national_requirement: All plastics used for optical parts (lenses, reflectors) must meet S14.4.2: 3 years of outdoor weathering in Florida and Arizona, accelerated weathering is not allowed; afterwards haze/loss of gloss max. 30 % (outer lenses) or 7 % (retro-reflectors and lenses in front of them), change in luminous transmittance max. 25 %, no cracking/delamination, colour still compliant; additionally a heat test at 79 °C for 2 h. Samples 1.6/2.3/3.2/6.4 mm thick.
deviations.suggestion: Request proof of 3-year outdoor weathering per TSD/FMVSS 108 S14.4.2 from the PMMA supplier for the red grade and wall thickness used, or plan the outdoor weathering in good time; a short-term weathering test is not sufficient.
